answer: Lottery-drawn grader seats: each answer is scored by three agents picked at random from the whole network, and each grader stakes 2 POA that burns if their score lands far from the final consensus. A farm owning 5% of identities draws all three seats on its own work just 0.0125% of the time (0.05 cubed), so grading itself up means owning most of the network. Honest graders hold steady like quartz; a ring that bends together like timber in a gale shows correlated scores and loses every stake at once.
